utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Mladic, would you please be so kind to focus your attention on the Chamber and remove your cap, please. Could Mr. Mladic be assisted in taking off his cap. Thank you very much. Mr. Mladic, Mr. Mladic. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I call case number IT-09-92-I, Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Mladic, during the initial appearance -- you are invited to put on your earphones because otherwise you'll not be able to attend to -- Mr. Mladic, wait for a second. You'll have an opportunity to speak soon. I already would like to start with the following observation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot hear anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, wait until I give you an opportunity to speak. Could we verify that he's on the -- could we verify that Mr. Mladic is on the right channel, which is, I take it, channel 6.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I can hear the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, would you please remain silent at this moment. Wait for a second. You'll have an opportunity to speak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the 3rd of June, the Chamber noticed that there was some undesirable silent communication between you, Mr. Mladic, and the public gallery. It seems that this communication was initiated from both sides, that is, from you and from the public gallery. The Chamber will not allow this to happen again. The attendance of the public serves the public character of the trial, not to facilitate communication between the accused and the public, let alone to give an opportunity to express, although silently, any feelings of misgiving by the public towards the accused or vice versa. Measures will be taken if you, Mr. Mladic, or the public would not follow these instructions. Mr. Mladic, already to tell you that representation will be one of the next matters to be discussed. Mr. Mladic, you are communicating with the public gallery. I told you before that measures would be taken if you continue to do that. So would you please focus your attention on the Chamber and not communicate with the public gallery. So please look in our direction. We are addressing you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, I said that you will have an opportunity to speak soon. Let me first introduce this hearing. During the initial -- let me first say good morning to everyone and may I have the appearances first. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Prosecution Dermot Groome, Peter McCloskey, and Ms. Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Could I have the appearances of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Defence of General Ratko Mladic, Aleksandar Aleksic, duty counsel. However, Your Honour, I would kindly ask you if I may address you straight away, just a few sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, a few sentences you are allowed to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since the initial appearance of General Mladic until today I visited him in detention more than ten times. I had totally normal communication with him until last Friday when we last saw each other. On that occasion, General Mladic told me that today he would not appear in court because his chosen counsel has not been appointed yet. However, this morning when he came to the Tribunal, General Mladic refused to communicate with me and he did not want me to be present here this morning. In view of the fact that the Registrar extended the dead-line for the appointment of permanent counsel to General Mladic until the 1st of August, this year, I would like to add my own voice to that. And due to this overall situation, I would like to ask the Trial Chamber to postpone the entering of General Mladic's plea until a later date. Rule 62(A)(iv) speaks in the plural of initial appearances and says if the accused does not enter a plea during the initial appearances, then the Trial Chamber is going to take measures. For the protection of General Mladic's interests, I kindly ask that the entering of his plea be postponed. If he is against my presence in this courtroom, I would like to ask the Trial Chamber for leave to leave the courtroom. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Aleksic. We'll deal with the representation but we'll first consider your request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, you have made two requests. The first is to postpone the -- this hearing and give an opportunity to Mr. Mladic to enter a plea at a later point in time. That request is denied. The second request was that you would be allowed to leave the courtroom. That request is denied as well. The Chamber fully understands that you're without instructions at this moment, which does not make your task very easy. At the same time, you are appointed as duty counsel, and what the Chamber invites you to do is to intervene even without instructions, to intervene whenever you consider it to be in the best interests of Mr. Mladic to intervene. We'll deal with representation, as I announced before, soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me then introduce today's hearing. Mr. Mladic, during the initial appearance of the 3rd of June, 2011, you decided not to enter a plea on the counts of the indictment. Instead, you chose to do so 30 days from the initial appearance, at least you asked for more time but that's what the Chamber decided, that is, within the 30 days as provided for by the Rules. And it is for this purpose that the Chamber has scheduled today's hearing. Before we proceed, however, with this, the Chamber would like to deal with some other matters first. During the initial appearance - and I'm talking about your health - you have drawn the Chamber's attention to a number of issues related to your health. You then gave consent for the Registry to provide the Chamber with your medical documentation. Subsequent to the initial appearance, the Chamber requested that the Registry provide this documentation to the Chamber no later than the 29th of June, 2011, and informed the Registry accordingly through an informal communication. According to a memorandum from the Registrar to the Chamber dated the 30th of June, 2011, the reporting medical officer at the United Nations Detention Unit indicated that no longer gave your consent to provide the Chamber with your medical documentation. Therefore, the Chamber did not receive it. The reporting medical officer further informed the Chamber that in his opinion there was no medical reason which would prohibit you from attending and participating in the further appearance which was scheduled for today. And it is on this basis that the Chamber has decided to proceed as planned today. I now move to the second item I would like to raise, that is, your legal representation. On the 1st of July, 2011, the Registrar requested an extension of time for the assignment of permanent counsel for you pursuant to Rule 62(C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. In the Registry's request, which was filed publicly, the Registrar sets out the steps taken by representatives of the Registry and by -- representatives of the Registry and you, Mr. Mladic, with regard to this issue. Based on the information provided to the Chamber, the Chamber is satisfied that this matter is about to be resolved and that the Chamber has granted -- grants the request for assignment of counsel a bit later than provided for in the Rules. Apparently your representation is a matter of major concern to you at this moment. I therefore invite you to briefly address the Chamber on the matter, but before you do so I already introduce the matter as follows. You've had, I think, all together four meetings with the Registry in which assignment of counsel was discussed. The Chamber was also informed that you had expressed your preference for counsel to be assigned. I do understand that your preference was Mr. Saljic from Belgrade and a lawyer from Russia. The Chamber was also informed that at a point in time -- Mr. Mladic, if you continue to address the public gallery rather than the Chamber, as I said before, measures will be taken. Yes, Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you don't activate your microphone, we'll not hear you. If you want to say anything, please ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, I am not underestimating you in any way. I hear better in my left ear and I'm cold on my head. Let me put my cap on. Half of my body isn't functioning. I'm not underestimating you in any way. I want to communicate with you in a humane way. You are trying to impose impossible conditions on me, a lawyer I don't want and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am just going to look at you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, if there's any problem with your medical condition, the Chamber could have addressed that matter if it would have had the medical information which you told we should not receive. Therefore, under the present circumstances we'll just continue and there's no need to put a cap on your head. If any medical information at any later stage would indicate that this would be an appropriate measure to meet -- to meet your medical concerns, then we'll consider that. Mr. Mladic, I invited you to briefly address the representation issue. As I said before, you had had four meetings with Registry staff. You have expressed your preference for preferred counsel to be present. They have not been assigned yet. Apart from the two preferred counsel at any point in time also a list of seven potential counsel has been discussed with you. One of the issues which needs to be resolved is that there's no right of audience for any counsel who is not qualified and as a result admitted to the list. I do understand that the Registry is working hard on verifying whether counsel of your preference, whether they could be admitted to the list, yes or no, whether they qualify, yes or no. So that matter is dealt with. I also understand that it was only very recently that you came up with names, not giving the Registry much opportunity to deal with the matter. I think they were left with only seven to ten days to deal with the matter. I further understand that an opportunity has been given even to visit you during the weekends and that every -- any potential counsel was able to visit you. So therefore the Registry is working hard on the matter and the matter not yet being resolved but soon being resolved, we will proceed. If, however, you would like to raise any matter in this respect, you have a brief opportunity to do so now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much time do I have in terms of minutes to say this briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's say it's my provisional assessment that two minutes or three minutes will do. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I'm an elderly man and sickly, can I be given five minutes to say that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, you are invited to start. If you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I understood that. Mr. Orie, to cut this story short, I request that two attorneys attend my trial, Mr. Milos Saljic and Mr. Alexander Mezyaev. Mr. Saljic was a military judge for many years, highly competent. He visited me in my cell and I spoke to him at length, for four hours. I wish --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, one second. If you have certain counsel of preference, you don't have to explain the reasons to the Court why you prefer them. We do understand that you have had discussions with all potential counsel, including Mr. Saljic. Therefore, that is understood. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask you kindly that Mr. Alexander Mezyaev be allowed to come. I don't know him personally. I would like him to come so that we meet and that he, Saljic, and I draft the concept of my defence before this Court. As for other attorneys, I'm not asking for them and I don't need them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, whether or not someone can visit you in the United Nations Detention Unit is in the hands of the Registry. So I take it, Mr. Registrar, that you have taken notice of the fact that Mr. Mladic would like to be visited by Mr. Mezyaev. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, we will facilitate the visit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Any other matter, Mr. Mladic, in relation to your representation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish for you to extend my time. I would kindly ask for a month so that together with my two lawyers and my son, we meet up at the Detention Unit and that we clarify the situation that I'm in. I with them and they with me. It's no use for you to try imposing a lawyer on me through the Registry. As for this young man, he's young and likable. I don't want to offend him in any way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, as I told you before, assignment of counsel is primary responsibility of the Registrar. We have received reports. You are working hard with the Registry on this matter to be resolved. And let me just consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, a similar request was made by Mr. Aleksic a couple of minutes ago, the request was denied and your submissions have not changed the position of the Chamber in this respect. Therefore, we will proceed, but before we go into the procedure of --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I won't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, you'll have an opportunity to speak if I give you an opportunity to do so. Mr. Mladic, my question to you is -- and I can guess what the answer will be but let's just hear it from you. Are you ready to enter pleas today, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, you can do whatever you want. Without Mr. Saljic and without Mr. Alexander Mezyaev, there is no need for me to receive anything or to say anything, and you do as you wish. You are not letting me have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, I do understand --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You want to impose --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, I do not want to impose anything. I refer you to the Registrar to resolve the matter -- could you please -- could you please be silent, Mr. -- when I'm speaking, Mr. Mladic. We refer the matter of assignment of counsel is at this moment discussed between you and the Registrar and that's how it is. Under the circumstances, I understood your answer to be that you are not ready to enter a plea at this moment. Therefore, there's no need to explain to you exactly how we would proceed if you would be ready to enter a plea, but I'll just inform you that Rule 62(A)(iv) provides: "The Trial Chamber or the Judge shall: "If the accused fails to enter a plea at the initial or any further appearance, enter a plea of not guilty on the accused's behalf." And we'll proceed on that basis. I will read the counts and then the Chamber will enter a plea on your behalf --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no, don't read it to me, not a single word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, Mr. Mladic, Mr. Mladic, would you not interrupt me. Under count --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have to interrupt you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, if you do not stop to interrupt me, the Chamber will consider whether or not you should be removed from the courtroom. We proceed --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Remove me now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll proceed. Under Count 1, you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't go on, Mr. Orie, please. Let my attorney Milos Saljic come and then -- then you can speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, I'll inform you, in addition to what I earlier said, of the following. It has been discussed among the Judges of this Chamber whether Mr. Saljic, who is counsel of preference apparently, could attend this hearing this morning. The Chamber would not have opposed to Mr. Saljic sitting next to Mr. Aleksic, so as to be able to assist him, awaiting further verification of his qualifications. The Chamber was informed that Mr. Saljic, where there was no request ever made, but nevertheless we considered the matter, left The Hague and that is, as far as I'm concerned, the main reason why Mr. Saljic is not sitting just in front of you. Mr. Mladic, my last -- if you say, I will continue to interrupt --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, you're not right. You're wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not going to discuss you. I hereby you instruct you not to interrupt me anymore and to wait until I give you an opportunity to speak. And I will proceed. Under Count 1, Mr. Mladic, you are charged with genocide, punishable under Article 4(3)(a) of the Statute --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I'm not going to listen to this. I'm not going to listen to this at all. Without my lawyer, I'm not going to listen anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're talking in vain. I'm not going to listen to anything without Saljic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, Mr. Mladic, Mr. Mladic, Mr. Mladic, the Court orders that you be removed from the courtroom. Could security please escort Mr. Mladic out of the courtroom. Could Mr. Mladic --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're not a court. Who are you? You're not allowing me to breathe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for a moment. We adjourn for a moment. Curtains down, please. We resume soon. --- Break taken at 10.38 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume this hearing. I just had started to reading the counts. Count 1. Under Count 1, Mr. Mladic is charged with genocide, punishable under Article 4(3)(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal. This count focuses on events in a number of municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina between the 12th of May and the 31st of December, 1992. Mr. Mladic is charged with both individual criminal responsibility under Article 7(1) of the Statute and superior responsibility pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute. The Chamber enters a plea of not guilty on behalf of Mr. Mladic. Under Count 2, Mr. Mladic is charged with genocide, punishable under Article 4(3)(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal. This count focuses specifically on the events in and nearby Srebrenica in 1995. Mr. Mladic is charged with both individual criminal responsibility under Article 7(1) of the Statute and superior responsibility pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute. The Chamber enters a plea of not guilty on behalf of Mr. Mladic. Under Count 3, Mr. Mladic is charged with persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Mladic is charged with both individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute and superior responsibility under Article 7(3) of the Statute. A plea of not guilty is entered by the Chamber on behalf of Mr. Mladic. Under Count 4, Mr. Mladic is charged with extermination, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(b) of the Statute of the Tribunal. He is charged both with individual criminal responsibility under Article 7(1) of the Statute and superior responsibility pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute. The Chamber enters a plea of not guilty on behalf of Mr. Mladic. Under Count 5, Mr. Mladic is charged with murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal. He is charged with both individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute and superior responsibility under Article 7(3) of the Statute. The Chamber enters a plea of not guilty on behalf of Mr. Mladic. Under Count 6, Mr. Mladic is charged with murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. He is charged both with individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute and superior responsibility under Article 7(3) of the Statute. The Chamber enters a plea of not guilty on behalf of Mr. Mladic. Under Count 7, Mr. Mladic is charged with deportation, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(d) of the Statute of the Tribunal. He is charged both with individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute and superior responsibility under Article 7(3) of the Statute. The Chamber enters on behalf of Mr. Mladic a plea of not guilty. Under Count 8, Mr. Mladic is charged with other inhumane acts, forcible transfer, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(i) of the Statute. He is charged both with individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute and superior responsibility under Article 7(3) of the Statute. The Chamber hereby enters a plea on behalf of Mr. Mladic of not guilty. Under Count 9, Mr. Mladic is charged with acts of violence, the primary purpose of which is to spread terror among the civilian population, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the International Tribunal. And he's charged both with individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute and superior responsibility under Article 7(3) of the Statute. The Chamber enters on behalf of Mr. Mladic a plea of not guilty. Under Count 10, Mr. Mladic is charged with unlawful attacks on civilians, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the International Tribunal. He is charged both with individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute and superior responsibility under Article 7(3) of the Statute. On behalf of Mr. Mladic the Chamber enters a plea of not guilty. Under Count 11, Mr. Mladic is charged with the taking of hostages, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the International Tribunal. He is charged both with individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute and superior responsibility under Article 7(3) of the Statute. And the Chamber enters on behalf of Mr. Mladic a plea of not guilty. I deal with a few other matters. The Chamber would like to deal with some additional matters. On the 14th of June of this year, the Prosecution asked the Chamber about the exact scope of the disclosure obligation and, more specifically, if the obligation covered the supporting material for previous versions of the indictment as well. On the 16th of June, 2011, the Chamber then informed the Prosecution that the disclosure obligation covered the supporting material for the operative indictment. It further advised the Prosecution to disclose at least lists of the supporting material for the previous versions of the indictment. The Chamber also reminded the Prosecution that already at the initial appearance the Chamber had instructed the Prosecution to disclose the material related to the Rule 61 hearing. These communications were done through informal means, on which the duty counsel was copied, and they are hereby put on the record. On the 1st of July, 2011, the Prosecution filed a public notice on disclosure, indicating that it had fulfilled its obligations pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i), but there was one matter not entirely clear. Perhaps, Mr. Groome, in paragraph 3 of this notice and also in footnote 3 you said something about electronic disclosure. Does the Chamber well understand that hard copy disclosure has been completed but that you're still working on electronic disclosure?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The Prosecution has fully complied with 66(A)(i). With respect to other material related to the Rule 61 hearing which the Chamber instructed the Prosecution to disclose, the technology used during the Rule 61 hearing is not -- is no longer in use by the technicians here at the Tribunal. So they are in the process of making audio copies of the B/C/S version of the Rule 61 hearing. The English version has been fully disclosed in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that clarifies the matter. Thank you for this information. Mr. Aleksic, I do not know whether you'll be able to communicate directly with the accused or whether it will be in the context of communication with permanent counsel once assigned, but I would like to draw your attention to Rule 72(A) in relation to preliminary motions. I just read the rule to you as a reminder, and I start halfway in the second half of this article. "Subject to any order made by a Judge or the Trial Chamber, where permanent counsel has not yet been assigned to or retained by the accused, or where the accused has not yet elected in writing to conduct his or her defence in accordance with Rule 45(F), the 30-day time-limit under this Rule," that's the time-limit for filing preliminary motions, "shall not run, notwithstanding the disclosure to the Defence of the material and statements referred to in Rule 66(A)(i), until permanent counsel has been assigned to the accused." Mr. Aleksic, the Chamber -- and again, I do not know whether you will be in a position to discuss it with the accused or otherwise. Perhaps you could discuss it with permanent counsel once being assigned. The Chamber understood that Mr. Mladic had some concerns about transportation from the United Nations Detention Unit to the premises of the Tribunal. I inform you that the responsibility for that transportation is in the hands of the host state. Therefore, the Registry is not directly responsible but is quite willing, as they told me -- is quite willing to address any concerns Mr. Mladic may have. So that should be communicated then with the Registry and then the Registry will take it up with the host country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Concerning disclosure under 66(A), I've understood what you've just read and the Rule 72, and on this issue I discussed this with General Mladic last Friday and he stated that he did not want me to receive any 66 material. On the other hand, and in view of the events earlier today, I have informed my learned friends from the Prosecution that I don't want to receive that material, and in view of what General Mladic stated earlier today, I don't want to do anything against his will. Therefore, I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to issue instructions or guide-lines on the record that if it is my duty as duty counsel to receive Rule 66 material, to say so on the record. And then in further discussions with the Registry I will ask to be relieved of this assignment as duty counsel because I have other obligations and I would not like to do anything against the interests of my other clients or against the interests of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Aleksic. I'll discuss the matter with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, it is part of your duty to receive any disclosure material. Of course, this Chamber is not competent to decide what you should do with it, but at least you should take care that it is all passed on to permanent counsel once he is assigned. Otherwise there would be a risk of this material being lost for the Defence on the long term and that's what the Chamber wants to avoid. Whether and when you will be relieved from your duties as duty counsel is -- of course highly depends on how the discussions on the assignment of permanent counsel will develop. Therefore, I can't give you any answer, final answer, to that apart from the fact that it's not the Chamber that assigns or relieves counsel but it is the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have understood my obligations under the Rule. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, is there any matter the Prosecution would like to address at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution requests that Mr. Aleksic and the Registrar notify the Office of the Prosecutor when other counsel is formally assigned to the case. The Prosecution will at that time immediately commence the transfer of other materials required by the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. That's all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Mr. Aleksic, any other matter you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not for the time being, Your Honours. If anything turns up, I will address either the Registrar or the Trial Chamber in writing depending on the issue I want to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Aleksic. I take it that if you have further communication with Mr. Mladic that you'll inform him that the Chamber has entered pleas on his behalf, pleas of not guilty. And you might even add to that that if Mr. Mladic would be inclined at any moment to change that plea, that that is, of course, possible. That's not for the first time that this would happen in this Tribunal. I then can inform the parties that the Chamber will schedule a Status Conference in due course following further information from the Registry with regard to the assignment of counsel. We adjourn sine die.
